newsitem.title: HAITI: Haitian elections postponed for second time.
newsitem.headline: Haitian elections postponed for second time.

text.p: Election officials announced on Thursday that second-round balloting in Senate elections scheduled for Sunday would be postponed indefinitely, the second time the vote has been put off.
The move came three days after the resignation of Prime Minister Rosny Smarth. Most of the major political parties had already announced they would boycott the ballot.
Haiti's Provisional Electoral Council (CEP) said at a news conference the vote would be put off until an as-yet undetermined date.
"The CEP needs to have further discussion with various political parties to guarantee fair elections," CEP Secretary General Alexandre Lavaud said.

The elections, to determine nine seats, one-third of the Senate, had initially been scheduled for May 25 but were delayed until Sunday. At the time, diplomatic sources attributed the delay to international pressure.

With most parties having decided to boycott the vote, the Party Fanmi Lavalas of former President Jean-Bertrand Aristide was virtually the only participant. The first round, on April 6, was dominated by Fanmi Lavalas.
Lavalas Political Organisation, the current ruling party, said last week it would boycott the election due to irregularities in the first-round vote count.
Another party, L'ouvri Barye announced on Wednesday that it would not participate.

"They took the president of the voting bureau in the South where complaints of fraud were the strongest and put him in my department (area)," Mary Lawrence Lasegue, the only female Senate candidate, said. "If I participate in these elections, it's like getting in to a car that has no brakes."

U.S. Embassy spokeswoman Meg Gilroy said the embassy had no immediate comment on the postponement. But she issued a statement noting that international elections observers had seen irregularities in the April 6 poll.

"The international community has expressed its concern to the CEP about the need to take a number of corrective technical measures to enhance the integrity of runoff elections and to ensure fairness," the statement said.

"Over the past year the Haitian government has taken steps toward economic modernisation," it said. "We hope that Haitian elected officials will maintain the momentum of these economic modernisation efforts."
In his resignation speech on Monday, Prime Minister Rosny Smarth criticised the CEP for trying to control the election results. "The CEP did not listen to any institutions, he said.
"They chose to act autonomously and do what they wanted despite protestations from several political parties."
"It is my position that elections cannot take place with such violations of the law and other incorrect actions," he said.

The nine Senate seats at stake are seen as key to the future of the U.S.-backed Haitian government plan to privatise state-run industries, including the electric and telephone companies. The Senate narrowly approved privatisation last year.
Aristide has spoken out against the privatisation plan and many Fanmi Lavalas candidates support his view on the issue.
